audit_findings.title: The earnings anchor predates a near-doubling of debt and may omit its current interest burden
audit_findings.magnitude: Debt increased $137.678 million, from $137.780 million at FY2025 to $275.458 million at July 4, 2026; quarterly interest expense increased $1.588 million year over year
audit_findings.mechanism: Incremental after-tax interest reduces equity-level owner earnings because debt principal is not deducted in the bridge
audit_findings.evidence: As of the end of fiscal 2025, cash and cash equivalents and restricted cash were $307 million, while debt, finance lease and other financing obligations were $138 million.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved mismatch, not a demonstrated error. The FY2025-based anchor may omit interest on the subsequently increased debt, although the July 2026 filing does not establish the sustainable debt balance, borrowing rate, or full-year after-tax burden. The available interest-expense increase is meaningful relative to the $151.3 million anchor but does not establish the recurring valuation effect.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $275.458 million obligations by component and rate, calculate normalized after-tax interest at the expected sustainable borrowing balance, and rerun all scenarios with owner earnings rebased for that expense.

audit_findings.title: Temporary tax benefits appear capitalized into the terminal period
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 tax expense was $15.133 million at an 8.0% rate; applying the filed 17%-19% FY2026 expectation to $188.018 million of FY2025 pretax income implies $16.830-$20.591 million of additional annual tax; the FY2025 tax-holiday benefit was $43.1 million and expires in 2034
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher normalized taxes reduce owner earnings, and expiration of the tax holiday reduces late-horizon and terminal cash flows
audit_findings.evidence: The annual effective tax rate for fiscal 2026 is expected to be approximately 17.0% to 19.0% assuming no changes to tax laws.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated structural omission because the stated valuation grows the historical owner-earnings anchor without an explicit tax schedule, while filed information shows both nonrecurring FY2025 benefits and a dated tax-holiday expiration. The FY2026 nine-month effective rate was already 19.0%. The indicated tax normalization is about 11%-14% of the $151.3 million anchor, and the $43.1 million holiday benefit is about 28% of it, making the issue capable of materially changing intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Remove the $8.2 million of identified FY2025 reserve and valuation-allowance releases, apply the filed FY2026 normalized tax-rate range, model global-minimum-tax effects, step taxes up when the APAC holiday expires in 2034, and rerun all scenarios and the buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may include customer-funded amounts that are not surplus equity cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to the $314.053 million cash bridge addition, or $11.44 per share; July 2026 customer advances were $602.933 million, including $424.6 million of inventory deposits and $164.5 million of deferred revenue
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required to fulfill customer-funded obligations or maintain operations should not be added as surplus cash in the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: As of September 27, 2025 and September 28, 2024, the balance of advance payments from customers attributable to deferred revenue was $ 151.3 million and $ 154.7 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved possibility rather than a demonstrated dollar-for-dollar error because the filing does not trace particular cash balances to customer advances or establish minimum operating liquidity. Nevertheless, the entire $314.053 million addition equals 11.7% of the $2.688 billion base equity value, so the uncertain excess-cash classification is potentially material.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile July 2026 cash to customer deposits, deferred revenue, restricted balances, foreign-cash accessibility, fulfillment requirements, and minimum operating liquidity; rerun the bridge using only cash demonstrated to be distributable and excess.

audit_findings.title: A known repatriation-tax cash claim may be missing from the latest bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum $16.5 million, or $0.60 per share and 0.6% of the $2.688 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: An unpaid tax obligation would reduce distributable cash in the equity bridge or future owner earnings
audit_findings.evidence: Our future cash flows from operating activities will be reduced by $16.5 million due to cash payments for U.S. federal taxes on the deemed repatriation of undistributed foreign earnings that are payable over an eight year period that began in fiscal 2019 and will end in fiscal 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the obligation remained unpaid on July 4, 2026 is unresolved, but even treating the entire filed $16.5 million as unpaid would reduce base value by only $0.60 per share. That is small relative to the $20.91 per-share bear-to-base scenario spread and cannot materially alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the fiscal 2026 payment date and amount from tax-payment records; if unpaid at the bridge date, deduct the remaining balance once without also reducing forecast owner earnings for the same payment.

audit_findings.title: The stated share ceiling may not capture maximum PSU payouts
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum incremental exposure is less than 0.5 million shares; adding the full 0.5 million as a conservative bound would increase the denominator 1.8% and reduce base value from $97.94 to approximately $96.19 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Above-target PSU issuance increases fully diluted shares and lowers intrinsic value per share
audit_findings.evidence: The number of shares that may be issued pursuant to PSUs ranges from zero to 0.5 million and is dependent upon the Company's TSR and economic return performance over the applicable performance periods.
audit_findings.explanation: The denominator includes the full 788,929 combined RSU/PSU inventory one-for-one, but the exact PSU portion and maximum incremental payout are unresolved. Even the conservative bound of adding another 0.5 million shares reduces per-share value by less than 2%, which is small relative to the scenario spread and market-price gap.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the current RSU/PSU split and award-level maximum payouts, remove any dilution already captured in the weighted-average share count, and recompute expected and maximum diluted shares.

audit_findings.title: Noncash finance-lease additions could escape the owner-earnings capital charge
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 finance-lease assets obtained were $6.015 million, equal to 6.3% of $95.264 million cash capital expenditures and 4.0% of the $151.3 million owner-earnings anchor; recurring valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back finance-lease amortization while omitting noncash acquisition or replacement cost would overstate owner earnings
audit_findings.evidence: Certain facilities and equipment held under finance leases are classified as property, plant and equipment and amortized using the straight-line method over the term of the lease and the related obligations are recorded as liabilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that noncash finance-lease additions occur, but the supplied record does not establish whether the owner-earnings maintenance-capex calculation already includes them or what portion represents recurring maintenance rather than growth investment. The known FY2025 amount is modest, but recurrence and terminal treatment could make the cumulative effect larger, so materiality remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the owner-earnings workpapers, identify finance-lease amortization added back and noncash additions omitted, classify maintenance versus growth additions, and rerun the valuation with an equivalent recurring lease-capital charge.
